title: Jabbo Smith and the orphan band
summary: Levy recognises Jabbo as the trumpeter he saw in the Jenkins orphan band. They talk about Jabbo's personality and restlessness.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Oh, later on he might have had it, yes. But I know when I first heard him. No, Jabbo, that was later. Yeah. Incidentally, do you know that Jabbo was in that little Cull of the Kids orphan band that came from the South? Yes, Jenkins. Yes. And I saw them, this is odd, I saw them on the street in Chicago when I first came here. They were a little bunch of kids. And there was one little guy there. He seemed to be in charge of everybody. He was a take charge guy. And he played the terrific trumpet. So years later, when I met Jabbo, and I went to rehearsal with his band, and I bought some of my arrangements. He wanted to use some of my arrangements, and later on he'd buy them. The more I looked at Jabbo, the more I began thinking. I said, listen. I said, did you ever play with a little kid's orphan band? And he almost jumped to the ceiling. He said, yes. I said, I remember him. I said, you were the trumpet player? And I said, I thought you were great. And he just slay on it and give him a big kick, see? And this is years later. It's funny how those things will come to you. Because I kept looking at him and thinking. And it, I don't know, this came to my mind. And now when I asked him, Jabbo had a lot of talent. And he had, he was a little bit peculiar. He, I don't know.

Well, being an orphan. Yeah. Being on his own all the time. Yeah. It was bound to affect his psychology. He wasn't as mellow as a lot of people. I don't think he is today. In fact, he doesn't even trust himself.

He comes down here, say, midnight or something like that, after he's through with a job in Milwaukee. And he won't go to bed for two days. Oh. There's a lot of things he wants to do around Chicago. Oh. We have a recording session. He's all played out. Played out, yes. Knocked out. Yeah, knocked out. And yet he'll keep on going another night. Yeah.
He loves to come down to Chicago. Uh-huh. He works at, a fellow his age just can't do it anymore.
Uh-huh. That's right. His age, yes.
